guitar.notes: Corrected: Chris Martin is the singer/pianist, not a guitarist credit worth listing alongside Buckland as primary guitarist; Jonny Buckland is the band's guitarist, mainly Fender Telecaster (sometimes Jaguar/Strat). Removed Martin and Martin-acoustic detail which conflated roles.

tone.target: bright anthemic clean-crunch with chorus and dotted delay
tone.profile: bright anthemic clean-crunch with chorus and dotted delay
tone.summary: A bright, chimey signal chain using a Fender-style amp (US Deluxe) for clean headroom, followed by Chorus and a light Overdrive boost to achieve the required 'edge breakup' sound, finished with Digital Delay and Room reverb.
corrections: keep the guitar bright and rhythmic

rig.name: Coldplay - Viva La Vida - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide subtle 'edge breakup' and warmth without heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used for light grit, simulating a clean boost/overdrive effect needed for the anthemic sound.
The target tone requires only light breakup, making a dedicated distortion unit unnecessary and potentially muddy.

blocks.purpose: Provide clean headroom and a bright, chimey foundation (Fender style).
Complement the US Deluxe amp model for a bright, articulate sound.
Add the required anthemic chorus effect.
Enhance the 'sparkly top end' and cut any potential muddiness.
blocks.gap: Used to fine-tune the frequency response for maximum brightness, as required by the target tone.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required 'dotted delay' effect (approximate time setting).
blocks.gap: Achieving a perfect dotted eighth note rhythm requires manual timing adjustment, but Digital Delay is the correct module.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle space and depth to the overall mix.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the bright, anthemic sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance clarity and brightness for anthemic pop-rock tone.
